workflows.name: Sync phone agent menu and hours with Decodo, Apify, DeepSeek and ElevenLabs
workflows.description:
An AI receptionist works until the lunch price moves or you close early for a holiday. Then it quotes the old menu with confidence, and the caller finds out when the food arrives. Owners in r/restaurantowners and r/smallbusiness say so often. This rebuilds the agent's knowledge each morning from your menu, pricing and FAQ pages plus your Google Business Profile, and touches ElevenLabs only when a price or an hour changed.

Last updated: November 2026.

Quick Overview
Decodo turns each page into markdown and keeps a failed page as a placeholder. Apify reads one Google Places record (name, address, phone, website, hours, rating, review count). DeepSeek V4.1 Flash merges both sides into one document with a fingerprint built from prices and hours, compared against the newest row for that agent. When it changed, the text goes to the ElevenLabs knowledge base, the agent is patched, and you get a voice note, a summary and a spoken preview of today's hours.

How it works
Daily 05:00 or Manual Sync Webhook (POST /sync-agent-knowledge) lands on Config: businessName, agentId, sourceUrls, googleMapsUrl, telegramChatId, voiceId, maxCharsPerPage, timezone, apifyActor.
Split Url List sends each URL to Decodo Scrape Page, a POST to data.decodo.com/v1/scrape for universal markdown, three retries. A failed page passes an empty result.
Trim Page Text keeps 6000 characters and swaps an empty page for "Page could not be loaded, ignore this source.", then Collect Pages builds one array.
Google Places Lookup runs the Apify compass~crawler-google-places actor on googleMapsUrl for one place, no reviews. Keep Safe Place Fields drops the rest.
Merge Sources pairs both lanes by position.
Write Knowledge Doc runs DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at 0.2 temperature with Knowledge Parser: contact details, hours, parking, menu prices as stated, policies, FAQ, and what it must not promise.
Get Version History reads rows for that agent_id, Only Last Version keeps one, and Knowledge Changed? compares fingerprints. A match ends at No Change Today.
Upload Knowledge Text posts to the Conversational AI knowledge-base endpoint, Attach To Agent PATCHes the agent with the new knowledge_base array, and Save Version stores the fingerprint and doc id.
Narrate Update, Send Update Notice and Narrate Hours Preview run together: a voice note with the change hint, a Telegram summary with the knowledge base id, and a voice note with today's hours.

Setup
Header Auth credential on Decodo Scrape Page with your Web Data API key.
Apify token on Google Places Lookup.
ElevenLabs API key on Upload Knowledge Text, Attach To Agent and both speech nodes.
Put your Conversational AI agent id in agentId. Config ships YOUR_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID, and nothing looks it up for you.
Replace businessName, sourceUrls, googleMapsUrl (your place CID), telegramChatId, voiceId, maxCharsPerPage and timezone.
Create a Data Table agent_knowledge_versions with agent_id, business_name, version_fingerprint, doc_id, changes_hint, version_date and pick it in both Data Table nodes.
Telegram bot credential on the three Telegram nodes and your chat id in Config.
Run the webhook once, read the summary, listen to the hours preview. Everything else is a Config edit.

Quick Answers
What about the agent's other documents?
Attach To Agent sends one item, so the PATCH replaces the whole knowledge_base list. Anything else that agent reads is lost unless you add it there too.

What if a page is down?
The scrape retries three times, then passes an empty result, so that page becomes the placeholder and the document uses the pages that answered. The Telegram notice shows the page count.

Does it rebuild the document every morning?
Only when the fingerprint changes. The Apify call still runs under its 0.5 USD cap, and unchanged prices and hours stop the run at No Change Today.

Can it answer allergen questions?
The document ends with what the agent must not promise, allergens included. DeepSeek still slips, so read a few transcripts in the first week.

workflows.name: Turn client voice notes into scoped briefs with DeepSeek, ElevenLabs and Apify
workflows.description:
A client sends a nine minute voice note about their site and half of it is about the weather. Typing the deliverables out of that note takes longer than reading a tidy email. This workflow turns the forwarded note into a scoped brief: the goal, deliverables with acceptance criteria, what is out of scope, the open questions and a 30 second readback you can forward for sign-off.

Last updated: November 2026.

Quick Overview
Forward the client voice note to a Telegram bot with an optional caption holding the business name and links. ElevenLabs scribe transcribes it with diarisation, DeepSeek pulls out only the facts, and each link is read as markdown through Decodo while Apify runs one Google Places lookup. DeepSeek writes the brief, Telegram sends it as text, ElevenLabs narrates the readback and Gmail mails you the brief and transcript.

How it works
Voice Brief In takes the message and downloads the audio. Voice Or Audio? passes only a voice note or audio file, and Reply Usage answers anything else.
First Time Seen? skips a message it already processed, keyed on chat id and message id.
Config holds the chat, your email, the voice, service type, rate, currency, language and caps.
Transcribe Note posts the file to ElevenLabs speech to text on scribe_v1 with diarisation. Extract Facts pulls client name, business, links and raw asks, and Facts Parser holds it to those fields.
Split Links, Limit Links and Links Found? walk the URLs to maxLinks. Scrape Page asks Decodo for markdown and Trim Page cuts each page to maxPageChars; No Pages keeps a linkless note alive.
Business Query builds the search string. Business Known? runs one Apify Google Places search capped at USD 0.50, and Business Facts keeps title, category, website, rating, reviews and address when the title matches.
Write Brief returns the goal, deliverables with acceptance criteria, out of scope, open questions, an hours estimate and a 70 to 85 word readback opening with "Here's what I understood". Brief Parser enforces that shape and Brief Output builds the text, email and caption.
Send Brief Text posts the brief. Narrate Readback voices it with ElevenLabs multilingual v2, Send Readback Audio sends the mp3 and Email Brief mails you the brief with the transcript.

Setup
Connect Telegram on Voice Brief In, Reply Usage, Send Brief Text and Send Readback Audio.
Connect ElevenLabs on Transcribe Note and Narrate Readback, then set voiceId in Config. The readback comes back as an mp3.
Connect Decodo as a Header Auth credential on Scrape Page, as the Authorization header.
Connect Apify on Apify Business with credit for compass~crawler-google-places, capped at USD 0.50.
Connect your DeepSeek credential on both model nodes, temperature 0.1 for facts and 0.3 for the brief.
Connect Gmail on Email Brief. It sends to freelancerEmail in Config, never to the client.
Fill in Config: freelancerEmail, serviceType, hourlyRate, currency and outputLanguage. serviceType feeds both prompts, hours times rate makes the price line, and the readback is spoken in outputLanguage.
Caps in Config: maxLinks 3, maxPageChars 4000, maxSpeechChars 4500, businessPlaceLimit 1, plus searchLanguage and searchCountry.
No sheet or table to create, the dedupe state lives in the Remove Duplicates node. Run one test note and check all three outputs.

Quick Answers
What happens if the same note arrives twice?
First Time Seen? drops a message with the same chat id and message id, so a redelivery does not run twice. A fresh forward gets a new id and runs again.
What if the note has no links or a page fails?
Links are optional. Split Links passes an empty list, No Pages hands a blank note on, and Scrape Page continues on error, so a dead URL only drops that page.
What happens if the narration fails?
Narrate Readback retries twice, then the run stops. The text brief reached Telegram first, but Email Brief runs after the audio, so no email goes out.

Additional info

workflows.name: Turn permit data into cleaning leads with Decodo, Apify, DeepSeek and ElevenLabs

user.name: Khairul Muhtadin
user.bio: Automation consultant & n8n Ambassador helping teams streamline sales, marketing and operations with AI-powered n8n workflows. Founder of Khaisa Studio and creator of 90+ ready-made n8n templates. Use my link to book a consultation for custom automation work.

workflows.description:
A cleaning company usually hears about a new office build-out weeks after the contractor hired someone. City permit feeds publish tenant improvement filings the day they are issued, while the space is bare and the contract undecided. This workflow reads that feed every weekday morning, matches each build-out to a business on Google Maps, scores the lead, and reads the best ones out loud before your first crew meeting.

Last updated: November 2026.

Quick Overview
Decodo fetches the last seven days of renovation and alteration permits from the feed URL, cost floor and keywords set in Config. Filter Permits keeps the ones above the cost floor that mention commercial space, and Skip Seen Permits drops repeats. Apify Google Maps looks up each address and returns the business name, phone, website and category, and DeepSeek scores the lead 1 to 10 with the likely use, the timing, a first line to say and the contact path. Leads go to a Google Sheet, the best few become a 45 second brief voiced with ElevenLabs, and Telegram and Gmail deliver it.

How it works
Weekday 07:00 runs Monday to Friday at 07:00, and Config builds the permit URL with a seven day window.
Fetch Permits with Decodo posts it to the web data API, Parse Permits reads the JSON, and Split Permits makes one item per permit.
Filter Permits keeps permits at or above minReportedCost whose work description matches a keyword.
Skip Seen Permits drops ids from earlier runs, Any New Permits? routes the rest, and Tell Nothing New answers an empty morning.
Limit Permits caps the batch at maxLeads, and Apify Google Maps searches each address with three results under a $0.50 charge ceiling.
Build Lead keeps the permit fields plus the first Maps match, One Lead Per Permit keeps one row per permit id, and Score Lead sends it to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.
Lead Parser returns lead_score, likely_use, why_now, outreach_line and contact_path. Lead Row shapes the row, Append Lead to Sheet writes it to a Leads tab, and Collect Leads gathers the run.
Write Morning Brief ranks by score and asks DeepSeek for 110 to 130 words. Narrate Brief voices it with ElevenLabs, Send Brief Audio posts the mp3, and Email Lead Table mails the table.

Setup
Add the Decodo key as a Header Auth credential with Authorization: Bearer .
Connect Apify on Apify Google Maps. apifyActor in Config defaults to compass~crawler-google-places.
Connect a DeepSeek credential (OpenAI compatible) on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Brief Model.
Connect ElevenLabs on Narrate Brief and pick the voice. voiceId and eleven_multilingual_v2 sit in Config.
Connect Telegram on Tell Nothing New and Send Brief Audio, and set telegramChatId.
Connect Google Sheets on Append Lead to Sheet, set sheetId, and make a Leads tab with columns runDate, permitId, permitNumber, issueDate, address, communityArea, reportedCost, workDescription, businessName, businessPhone, businessWebsite, businessCategory, mapsRating, mapsReviews, leadScore, likelyUse, whyNow, outreachLine, contactPath.
Connect Gmail on Email Lead Table and replace user@example.com with your address.
Check permitsUrl and city. The default is Chicago dataset ydr8-5enu, and any Socrata feed with these field names works.
Run one test with maxLeads at 1 or 2 to check the Maps match and sheet row first.

Quick Answers
Does it chase the same permit twice?
Skip Seen Permits remembers permit ids from earlier runs, so each job goes out once.

What happens on a day with no new permits?
Tell Nothing New sends one Telegram line with the date and cost floor; nothing reaches Apify.

How much Apify credit can one morning burn?
maxLeads caps the addresses, each search returns three results, and the run stops at a $0.50 charge.

What if no business shows up at that address?
Build Lead writes "No business found at this address", and the scoring prompt tells the model not to invent one: why_now says the lookup was empty and contact_path points at the site office or the general contractor on the permit. Check a listed phone before calling it a prospect.

workflows.name: Save new LinkedIn job-based B2B sales leads to Google Sheets with Apify
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Discover potential B2B sales opportunities through LinkedIn hiring activity. This workflow runs daily, scrapes recent job postings using Apify, filters out previously collected jobs, saves new leads to Google Sheets, and sends a Slack notification.

How it works
Runs every day at 08:00 on a schedule.
Uses the Apify Scraper to collect up to 100 recent job postings matching your selected job titles and location.
Removes previously collected jobs and duplicate job IDs within the current execution.
Checks whether any new job leads remain. If no new leads are found, the workflow stops without sending a notification.
Appends each new job record to Google Sheets with company details, job information, posting metadata, and lead status.
After the spreadsheet update succeeds, sends one Slack message summarizing the newly discovered leads, including company names, job titles, locations, and job links.

Setup
Connect your Apify account in n8n and ensure you have access to the Rapid LinkedIn Scraper Actor.
Connect your Google Sheets OAuth2 credentials and select the spreadsheet and worksheet used to store job leads.
Connect your Slack account and configure the channel where new lead notifications should be delivered.
Configure the Apify input with your target job titles, location, maximum number of results, and posting date range.
Ensure your Google Sheets worksheet contains the required column headers, especially job_id, which is used to identify previously collected jobs.
Test the workflow to verify scraping, duplicate detection, spreadsheet updates, and Slack notifications before activating the daily schedule.

Requirements
An n8n instance with permission to install community nodes.
Apify account with access to the Rapid LinkedIn Scraper Actor.
Apify community node (@apify/n8n-nodes-apify) installed in n8n.
Google account with access to Google Sheets.
Slack workspace and permission to post messages in the selected channel.
A Google spreadsheet with the required job lead columns.

Customization
Job titles: Replace the default job titles with roles relevant to your target customers.
Location: Change the geographic location to focus on your preferred market.
Result limit: Adjust the maximum number of job postings collected per execution.
Posting date: Monitor jobs posted within the past 24 hours, past week, or past month.
Google Sheets: Customize the spreadsheet columns to match your prospecting process.
Slack notifications: Change the destination channel and customize the notification message.
Lead qualification: Extend the workflow with AI-powered company research, lead scoring, or CRM integrations.

Additional info
This workflow helps identify potential B2B sales opportunities by monitoring companies' hiring activity on LinkedIn. Hiring for specific roles can indicate business growth, new projects, or potential demand for relevant products and services.

Potential use cases:
SaaS companies discovering businesses that may need their products.
B2B sales teams identifying potential customers.
Marketing and lead generation agencies finding growing businesses.
Consultants monitoring companies hiring for relevant roles.
Business development teams tracking hiring activity in target markets.
The workflow stores newly discovered job postings in Google Sheets and sends a Slack notification after successfully saving new leads. Existing job IDs are checked to prevent previously collected jobs from being added again.

You can customize job titles, locations, result limits, posting date ranges, Google Sheets destinations, and Slack notifications according to your prospecting requirements.

Resources:

Rapid LinkedIn Scraper: https://apify.com/worldunboxer/rapid-linkedin-scraper

Apify n8n Integration Documentation: https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/n8n

n8n Documentation: https://docs.n8n.io/

workflows.name: Enrich company website rows in Google Sheets with Apify contacts data

Quick overview
This manual workflow reads a Google Sheets list of company websites, enriches each site with emails, phone numbers, LinkedIn URL, and detected technologies using the Apify Company Contacts & Tech Stack Lookup actor, then writes the results back to the same sheet.

How it works
Starts when you run the workflow manually.
Reads rows from Google Sheets and keeps only those with a non-empty website and an empty status to avoid reprocessing.
Groups the remaining websites into batches and limits how many rows are handled per run.
Sends each batch to Apify (Company Contacts & Tech Stack Lookup actor) to extract company contacts and the site’s technology stack with a spend cap per batch.
Matches Apify results back to the original Google Sheets row numbers, optionally flags whether a specified technology is present, and formats the output fields.
Updates the Google Sheets rows with status, company name, best email, emails, phones, LinkedIn URL, technologies, and the uses_tool flag.

Setup
Create an Apify account, add an Apify API token in n8n, and ensure you can run the “Company Contacts & Tech Stack Lookup” actor.
Add a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential in n8n and select it for both Google Sheets steps.
Prepare a Google Sheet with headers: website, status, companyName, bestEmail, emails, phones, linkedinUrl, technologies, uses_tool, and paste your sheet URL and tab name into the workflow settings.
Adjust batchSize, maxRowsPerRun, maxPagesPerSite, maxCostPerRunUsd, and (optionally) toolToFlag to control throughput, spend, and technology flagging.

user.name: Magnova

Simple pay-per-event pricing with no start fees—ready to connect straight to Google Sheets, Slack, and AI pipelines. Browse all our Actors & video tutorials via the link below.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs daily to search recent USPTO trademark filings via Apify for a given wordmark, then logs newly seen matches to Google Sheets and posts alerts to Slack, while suppressing notifications on the first run by establishing a baseline of previously found serial numbers.

How it works
Runs every day on a schedule trigger.
Sets the target brand keyword and calculates a “filed after” date for the last 90 days.
Uses Apify to run the USPTO Trademark Search actor and return live trademark filings matching the keyword.
Compares each result’s serial number against stored history to keep only filings that have not been seen before, and on the first run returns a baseline message instead of alerts.
If it is the baseline run, posts a “baseline established” message to a Slack channel.
Otherwise, appends each new filing to Google Sheets and posts a formatted Slack alert with the TSDR link to the official USPTO record.

Setup
Add an Apify API token credential and ensure the workflow can run the USPTO Trademark Search actor (ID: I8KvtBliDeyVghVzU).
Update the monitored keyword by replacing YOUR BRAND in the brand setting.
Connect your Google Sheets account, set the target spreadsheet URL/ID, and create a sheet with headers: Wordmark, Owner, Status, Filed, Serial number, Registration number, TSDR link.
Connect your Slack account and set the alert channel (for example, #trademark-alerts) for both Slack messages.
Run the workflow once to establish the baseline, then activate it for ongoing daily monitoring.

workflows.name: Log weekly Google Trends for keyword lists with Apify and Google Sheets
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs every Monday and reads a keyword list from Google Sheets, fetches Google Trends interest-over-time data for the list via Apify, then writes one weekly summary row per keyword (latest complete week and average) back to a Trends sheet.

How it works
Runs on a schedule every Monday at 07:07 in the workflow time zone.
Reads keywords from the keyword column in the Keywords tab of Google Sheets, trimming, deduplicating, and stopping if the list is empty.
Sends the keyword list, country (geo), and time range to the Apify Google Trends actor to fetch interest-over-time results in a single run.

A Google account with Google Sheets

user.name: Paolo Ronco
user.bio: Cybersecurity Analyst exploring the intersection of automation, cloud computing, and artificial intelligence. I build and experiment with n8n workflows, API integrations, and AI-powered solutions, focusing on practical applications, efficiency, and reliable system integration.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
Turn Telegram messages into an organized Notion knowledge inbox. Capture Instagram posts and Reels, TikTok videos, YouTube videos and Shorts, webpages, screenshots, or quick ideas. OpenAI extracts key information, creates concise English summaries, and suggests relevant next steps while preserving source context.

How it works
Capture:* A Telegram bot receives messages from an authorized user and identifies the source type.
Extract:* Dedicated branches retrieve Instagram carousel images or video transcripts, TikTok transcripts, YouTube captions or speech-to-text, public webpage text, and screenshot content. Plain-text ideas are preserved directly.
Analyze:* OpenAI produces a searchable title, short summary, key takeaways, optional details, and up to three evidence-based tasks in a structured format.
Organize:* The workflow creates a Notion Inbox page with category, source information, original message, and relevant content blocks.
Confirm:* Telegram returns a link to the saved page. Unsupported inputs and processing failures receive a helpful reply instead.

Setup
Import* the workflow JSON into n8n.
Telegram:* Connect your bot credentials to the trigger and reply nodes. Set your authorized user ID in Telegram — Receive Message.
OpenAI:* Connect an API credential to the chat model and Vision nodes; confirm the configured model is available to your account.
Apify:* Configure HTTP Header Auth for the Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube actors used by the workflow.
Notion:* Create or select an Inbox database, grant the integration access, and configure the database ID, property IDs, status option, and mappings in Notion — Prepare Inbox Page.
Check the schema:* The supplied mapping expects a title, status, type, category, source URL, and date property. The categories are AI, Cyber, Tech, and Lifestyle; source types include Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, website, Screenshot, and Idea.
Test and activate:* Verify one message per supported source, an invalid link, and a failed extraction. Make sure no other active workflow is using the same Telegram bot webhook.

Requirements
n8n** instance capable of receiving Telegram webhooks.
Telegram** bot token and authorized user ID.
OpenAI** API access for structured text analysis and image understanding.
Apify** account, API token, and access to the configured scraping/transcription actors.
Notion** integration with permission to create pages in the destination database.
Publicly accessible source content for external extraction; usage-based API charges may apply.

Customization
AI instructions:** Edit AI — Build Prompt to change language, summary length, categories, takeaways, and task-generation rules.
Output schema:** Update Structured Output Parser and the corresponding Notion page preparation logic together.
Notion layout:** Adjust properties, headings, content blocks, and task formatting in Notion — Prepare Inbox Page.
Sources:** Extend Telegram — Classify Message and Telegram — Route by Type with additional processing branches.
Feedback:** Customize help, success, and error messages in Reply — Format Message.
Limits:** Review Apify run limits, transcript handling, image constraints, and extraction timeouts before changing them.

Additional info
One message, one entry:** Only the first URL is processed; Telegram albums are handled as separate messages.
English output:** Generated Notion content is in English, regardless of the source language. Original source information is retained where available.
Instagram:** Public Reels, photo posts, and carousels are supported; carousel analysis uses up to 20 ordered images or previews.
YouTube:** Videos and Shorts use available captions or AI speech-to-text. Very long transcripts may be sampled across the video.
TikTok:** Public video transcription supports up to 300 seconds of audio.
Images:** Telegram image attachments must be under 10 MB; unreadable text is not guessed.
Extraction limits:** Video visuals are not analyzed. Dynamic, private, login-protected, or unavailable pages may not yield usable text.
Tasks:** Suggested next steps are labeled as suggestions, not commitments. No persistent deduplication is implemented.
Reliability:** The bot confirms a successful save only after Notion returns a page ID. External services can fail or incur charges.

Full technical documentation: Notion — Telegram Second Brain

Reads the Products tab in Google Sheets and keeps only rows where Product is filled and Status is empty.

Add a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential and select it in the three Google Sheets steps, then paste your sheet URL into the Settings values.
Add an Apify API token as an HTTP Header Auth credential (Authorization: Bearer YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN) and select it for the Apify request.
Adjust Settings values such as offersPerProduct, maxMoq, sortBy, and the cnyToUsd exchange rate to match your needs.

A free Apify account (the free plan includes monthly credits) and a Google account with Google Sheets.

Customization
Change the schedule, the number of offers per product, the maximum MOQ or the exchange rate in the Settings node; switch sortBy to rank by sales instead of price.

workflows.name: Monitor domain expiry, SSL and email security with Apify and Google Sheets
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs every Monday to check a list of domains using Apify Domain Intelligence, then writes registrar, domain and SSL expiry, email security (SPF/DMARC), and website status into Google Sheets with an Issues column that flags problems.

How it works
Runs every Monday at 08:00 on a schedule.
Sends the configured domain list to Apify Domain Intelligence and retrieves DNS, SSL, email, and website status details.
Keeps only results that are valid domain reports and ignores non-domain/error rows.
Builds a per-domain Issues summary (expiry warnings, SSL trust/expiry, SPF/DMARC gaps, and website errors) and formats the remaining fields for reporting.
Appends new rows or updates existing rows in Google Sheets by matching on the Domain column.

Setup
Create an Apify account, generate an API token, and add an HTTP Header Auth credential that sets Authorization: Bearer  for the Apify request.
Update the domain list and warnDays threshold in the workflow to control what gets checked and when expiry warnings appear.
Connect Google Sheets, paste your spreadsheet URL and pick the tab. The first row needs these headers: Domain, Issues, Registrar, Domain expires, Days to expiry, SSL expires, SSL days left, Email provider, SPF, DMARC policy, HTTP status, Final URL, Last checked. After picking the tab, n8n resets the mapping: set Mapping Column Mode back to Map Automatically and Column to match on to “Domain”.

Requirements
An Apify account (the free plan's monthly credit covers small lists; the Domain Intelligence Actor costs about $5 per 1,000 domain checks) and a Google account with Google Sheets.

Customization
Change warnDays, run daily instead of weekly, or add a Filter on Issues != "OK" followed by Slack, Gmail or Microsoft Teams to get alerted only when something needs attention.

Additional info
Registration data comes from RDAP, the official successor to WHOIS; some country domains (for example .io and .es) don't publish it, so their registrar and expiry stay empty. DMARC is only flagged for domains that receive email. One run must finish within 5 minutes, which covers a few hundred domains. Tested on n8n 2.46.6. workflows.name: Find course gaps from LinkedIn jobs with OpenAI, Apify and Slack
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Find the skills employers keep asking for that the LinkedIn Learning course catalog barely covers. Each month it reads LinkedIn postings for your roles, has AI name the skills, counts them in the text, checks the catalog, and drafts a course idea per gap for Google Sheets and Slack.

How it works
A monthly schedule starts the run, and a Set node holds your roles, the place and the gap rules.
The first Actor searches LinkedIn jobs for each role and returns LinkedIn's own job count for the month.
The same Actor reads every posting in full. Reposts with identical text are kept once.
An Information Extractor names the 20 most common skills and the exact words the postings use for each.
A Code node counts how many postings mention each skill, overall and per role. Skills above your cut-off in any role go to the catalog check.
The second Actor searches the LinkedIn Learning catalog for every in-demand skill in one run.
A Code node counts the courses whose title names the skill and finds the newest one. Few courses, or only old ones, is a course gap.
A second Information Extractor drafts a course idea for each gap from lines in the postings. Every skill goes to Google Sheets, and the top gaps go to Slack.

Setup
Create a free Apify account, copy the API token from Settings, Integrations, and add it as an Apify credential on the three Actor nodes.
Add an OpenAI credential on the two chat model nodes, or swap in any other chat model.
Connect Google Sheets and pick a spreadsheet and tab. The columns are created from the first rows.
Connect Slack and pick a channel for the digest.
Put your roles and place in the Set node, run it once by hand, then activate it.

Requirements
An Apify account; a month of three roles costs about one cent in Actor charges
An OpenAI API key, or any chat model credential n8n supports
Google Sheets and Slack credentials
No LinkedIn account, LinkedIn Learning license or scraping key

Customization
roles takes any comma-separated list of job titles; one search runs per role
postingsPerRole sets how many postings are read per role; more give steadier shares
minShare is the share of postings a skill needs in at least one role to be checked
thinCourses and staleYears decide what counts as a gap: too few courses, or none recent enough
ideasInSlack caps how many course ideas the digest shows
Swap Slack for the optional Gmail node, or add the optional details read for the closest course's ratings and syllabus

Additional info
How do I find course ideas that people will pay for? Start from what employers ask for, then check what already exists. This template reads recent LinkedIn postings for the roles your audience wants, counts the skills those postings mention, and searches the LinkedIn Learning course catalog for each one. A skill that many postings want and few courses teach is a course gap. That's the topic to build first.

How is a gap decided? A course counts only when its title names the skill, because the catalog search is loose: "go-to-market strategy" reports hundreds of results, but in our test only one course had it in its title. A skill with two or fewer such courses, or none released in the last three years, is a gap. Both limits sit in the Set node. When no title names the skill, the row shows the closest course so you can judge the near miss yourself.

Can I trust the numbers? The model only names the skills and drafts the course ideas. Code does the counting, so "8 of 20 postings" means 8 posting texts contain the words, and "1 course names it" is a count of real catalog rows. A skill the model names but no posting uses is marked Not in the postings and never reaches the catalog check. An idea for a skill that is not on the gap list is dropped.

Why is one employer not counted three times? Companies often post the same job in several cities with identical text. The workflow keeps one copy of each description before counting, so a single employer's reposts don't make a skill look popular.

Who is it for? Course creators and instructors choosing their next topic, bootcamps checking a syllabus against the market, L&D teams deciding what to buy or build, and training companies that sell to one industry. Put the roles your learners want in the Set node.

What does it cost? Every posting, listing and course costs $0.00001, so three roles at ten postings each, plus twelve catalog searches, come to about one cent a month in Apify charges. The two model calls cost a few cents on gpt-5-mini. A run takes a few minutes.

What else can these Actors do? LinkedIn Job Search Scraper is a LinkedIn job scraper and job search API in one: keyword and place search with date and company filters, full job descriptions, result counts, and title, company and location autocomplete, all without a LinkedIn login. LinkedIn Learning API searches the LinkedIn Learning course catalog by keyword, topic, level, length and software, and returns full course records with ratings, reviews, syllabus and learning paths.

About Apify. LinkedIn Learning API runs on Apify, a platform of ready-made scrapers and APIs for sources that have no usable public API. Actors are pay per use with no subscription, and they run in the cloud, so nothing runs on your machine and nothing breaks when the source changes its markup.

New to Apify? You can set up a free account and get the API token this template needs in a couple of minutes.

workflows.name: Plan 30-day LinkedIn Learning onboarding with Apify, OpenAI and Slack
workflows.description:
Quick overview
A manager adds a new hire on a form. This finds their public LinkedIn profile, searches LinkedIn Learning for each skill the role needs, has AI pick one course per skill, and spreads the courses over four weeks. The plan goes to the manager in Slack and to Google Sheets.

How it works
The built-in n8n form takes the new hire's name, previous employer, optional profile URL, role, start date and the manager's Slack member ID.
A Set node holds your role list, one line per role with its skills in teaching order, and the study hours per week.
A role that isn't on the list gets one logged row and a Slack note to the manager instead of a guessed plan.
The first Actor searches public LinkedIn profiles by name and previous employer. A pasted URL wins, otherwise only an exact full-name match counts.
The second Actor reads the public profile. Not found, a failed search or an unreadable profile still produces a plan with every skill in it.
The third Actor searches the LinkedIn Learning course catalog for all the skills in one run, five courses each.
The Information Extractor picks the best course for each skill by its number and copies any words from the profile that show the person already has a skill.
A Code node rejects quotes that aren't on the profile and numbers that aren't on the list, then fills weeks 1 to 4 within your study-hours budget.
Google Sheets gets one row per skill, and the manager gets one Slack direct message grouped by week.

Setup
Create a free Apify account, copy the API token from Settings, Integrations, and add it as an Apify credential on the three Actor nodes.
Add an OpenAI credential on the chat model node, or swap in any other chat model.
Connect Google Sheets and pick a spreadsheet and tab. The columns are created from the first rows.
Connect Slack. Managers find their member ID under their Slack profile, More, Copy member ID.
Edit the role list and the weekly hours in step 2, then activate the workflow and share the form URL with your managers.

Requirements
An Apify account; the free tier covers many new hires a month
An OpenAI API key, or any chat model credential n8n supports
Google Sheets and Slack credentials
A LinkedIn Learning license for the new hire to watch the courses
No LinkedIn login, no LinkedIn Learning admin API and no HR system

Customization
roleSkills is your role list: one line per role, a colon, then the skills in the order you want them taught
hoursPerWeek sets how much course time goes into each of the four weeks; anything that does not fit is listed as After day 30
Start from your HR system instead of the form with the optional webhook and field mapping at the bottom of the canvas
Send the plan to a channel, Microsoft Teams or email instead of a Slack direct message
Add the course details read from the LinkedIn Learning Actor to bring ratings and syllabus into each row

Additional info
How do I build an onboarding training plan from LinkedIn Learning? Keep a short skill list for each role you hire for. When someone joins, this template searches the LinkedIn Learning course catalog for every skill on their role's list, picks the course that fits each one, and lays the courses out over the first 30 days at a pace you set, three hours a week by default. The manager gets the plan before day one.

Does it read the new hire's LinkedIn profile to tailor the plan? Yes, but carefully. Public profiles show a short about line, the current employer, education and awards, and almost never a skills list. So every skill stays in the plan by default. The model can skip a skill only by quoting words from the profile that show it, and a Code node drops the skip if those words aren't on the profile word for word. Skipped skills are listed in the Slack message with the quote, so the manager can disagree.

Are the courses real? Yes. Every course comes from a live search of the LinkedIn Learning course catalog, with its title, length and link. The catalog search is loose ("pipeline management" also returns data engineering courses), so the model chooses from the five results by number with the role in view, and may answer none. A number that isn't on the list is rejected. A skill with no fitting course says Pair with a teammate instead of showing a course that doesn't teach it.

What happens when the person can't be found? The search uses the name and previous employer and only accepts an exact full-name match, because a name search can also return their colleagues. If nobody matches, the plan still goes out with every skill in it and says the profile wasn't found. Paste the profile URL on the form to skip the guesswork.

What does it cost per new hire? Apify charges are under a cent, most of it the people search at $0.0006 per person found. Each profile and each course costs $0.00001. One model call is about a cent on gpt-5-mini. A run takes one to three minutes.

LinkedIn Profile API reads up to 1,000 public profiles in one run. LinkedIn Learning API searches the LinkedIn Learning course catalog and returns full course records with ratings, reviews, syllabus and learning paths. If you self-host n8n, n8n-nodes-linkedin-profile-api wraps the Profile Actor as a community node.

workflows.name: Shortlist LinkedIn candidates from competitors with Apify, OpenAI and Slack

Quick overview
Open a role in a form and get a scored candidate shortlist in Slack. It maps your competitors' teams on LinkedIn, searches the role in your city, reads each public profile, and has AI score everyone against your job description, quoting the profile. Every candidate lands in Google Sheets.

How it works
The built-in n8n form takes the role title, the job description, a city and a list of competitor companies.
A Set node holds your company name, people per company, the search size, the shortlist size and the score cut-off.
The first Actor maps each competitor team by title and city, and confirms each person currently works there. At the same time, the second Actor searches LinkedIn for the same title in the same city.
A Code node merges both lists into one row per profile, drops your own people, and notes any competitor that came back empty.
The third Actor reads every public profile in one call. It adds about text, past employers, schools and awards.
The Information Extractor scores each candidate 0 to 100 against the job description and quotes the phrase on the profile that backs the score.
A Code node ranks everyone. A score only counts when its quote is really on the profile. If it isn't, the candidate goes to Check by hand, never onto the shortlist.
Every candidate goes to Google Sheets. Slack gets one message per role: the top five at or above the cut-off, or why there is no shortlist and who came closest.

Setup
Create a free Apify account, copy the API token from Settings, Integrations, and add it as an Apify credential on the three Actor nodes.
Add an OpenAI credential on the chat model node, or swap in any other chat model.
Connect Google Sheets and pick a spreadsheet and tab.
Connect Slack and pick the channel on both Slack nodes.
Put your company name in the Set node so your own employees are skipped.
Activate the workflow and share the form URL from the trigger node with your recruiting team.

Requirements
An Apify account; the free tier covers several roles a month
An OpenAI API key, or any chat model credential n8n supports
Google Sheets and Slack credentials
No LinkedIn Recruiter seat, cookies, Google search API key or data vendor contract

peoplePerCompany sets how deep each competitor team is mapped; five is plenty for a first shortlist
shortlistScore and shortlistSize decide who reaches Slack, without touching the prompt
Add comma-separated title keywords in the form to catch other titles for the same job

workflows.name: Score LinkedIn buying intent with OpenAI, Apify, Google Sheets and Slack
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Every morning this runs LinkedIn post search on the phrases your buyers use, like "recommend a bookkeeper". AI sorts real buyers from the vendors using the same words. Every post is logged to Google Sheets, and buyers above your intent bar reach Slack with their profile and a draft reply.

How it works
A Schedule trigger runs every morning at eight.
A Set node holds what you sell, who buys it, the buyer phrases, the search window and your intent bar.
The first Actor searches public LinkedIn posts for each phrase over the past week.
A Code node keeps one item per post. If there are no posts and the search reported an error, a Slack warning goes out instead. A quiet day sends nothing.
Remove Duplicates skips posts that were seen on an earlier run.
The Information Extractor labels each post as buyer, seller, job seeker or other. It also scores intent from 0 to 10, names the need, says why, and drafts a reply.
A Code node decides whether to alert using your intent bar, and every post is appended to Google Sheets.
Buyers who post from a personal profile are looked up in one call to the second Actor for their current company and location.
Slack gets one alert per buyer with the post excerpt, the draft comment and the link.

Setup
Create a free Apify account, copy the API token from Settings, Integrations, and add it as an Apify credential on both Actor nodes.
Add an OpenAI credential on the chat model node, or swap in any other chat model.
Connect Google Sheets and pick a spreadsheet and tab.
Connect Slack and pick a channel on both Slack nodes.
In the Set node, describe what you sell and who buys it, and list five to ten phrases your buyers write when they ask for help.
Activate the workflow.

Requirements
An Apify account; the free tier covers daily runs for a small phrase list
An OpenAI API key, or any chat model credential n8n supports
Google Sheets and Slack credentials
No LinkedIn account, cookie or social listening subscription

Customization
phrases are searched one by one. Write them the way a buyer asks, not the way a vendor sells
minIntent sets how sure the model must be before Slack hears about it; the sheet still logs every post
postedWithin set to week with a daily run catches posts that LinkedIn indexes late; use month for a weekly run
maxPostsPerPhrase caps cost and run time per phrase
Add the optional company lookup (LinkedIn Company API) before the alert for company size and industry
Add the optional country filter to alert only on buyers in the markets you serve

Additional info
How do I find people on LinkedIn asking for recommendations? List the phrases a buyer would write, such as "looking for a fractional CFO" or "can anyone recommend a CRM". The template runs a LinkedIn post search for each phrase every morning and keeps the posts from the past week. You don't need a LinkedIn account, and the people asking for what you sell show up the morning they post.

Is this LinkedIn social listening without a login? Yes. Both Actors read public LinkedIn pages, so you never connect an account or paste a cookie. If you want the raw feed, the post search works as a small social listening API that returns one row per post with its text, author, date, reactions and comments.

Why not alert on every post that matches? Most of them are not buyers. On our test run, 8 of the 11 posts that matched buyer phrases came from accountants, bookkeepers, tutors and firms marketing their own services, in the same words a buyer would use. The model reads each post and labels the author, so Slack only hears about people asking for help. The sheet keeps every post with its verdict, so you can check the model's calls and tune your phrases.

How is buying intent scored? The model gets what you sell, who buys it, and one short card per post. It returns a role (buyer, seller, job seeker or other) and an intent score from 0 to 10, where 9 or 10 means asking for recommendations or quotes now. A post saying the need is already filled scores low. The alert decision comes from your own intent bar, not from the model.

Does it tell me who the buyer is? Mostly. For buyers posting from a personal profile, one call to the profile Actor adds their current company, location and the first line of their About section. A buyer posting as a company page still gets an alert, without the profile details.

What does it cost? With five phrases, a daily run costs about 2 cents in Apify charges on a paid plan and about 7 cents on the free plan, plus one small model call per new post. Posts and search pages seen again within seven days come from a cache and are not charged. A failed search is never charged.

What else can these Actors do? LinkedIn Post Search API finds public LinkedIn posts and articles by keyword, name or hashtag, for any date range. LinkedIn Profile API returns public profile data, such as current company, experience, education and followers. If you self-host n8n, n8n-nodes-linkedin-profile-api wraps the profile Actor as a community node.

About Apify. LinkedIn Post Search API runs on Apify, a platform of ready-made scrapers and APIs for sources that have no usable public API. Actors are pay per use with no subscription. They run in the cloud, so nothing runs on your machine, and nothing breaks when the source changes its markup.

user.name: Hanna Nosova

workflows.description:
Catch regressions, security reports and breaking changes in the open-source libraries you depend on before they reach your users. Each weekday this template fetches new and updated issues from the GitHub repositories you list, using the FetchCat GitHub Issues & Pull Requests Scraper on Apify. No GitHub login is needed. One OpenAI call scores each issue for upgrade and production risk, every issue is logged to Google Sheets, and only the high-risk ones are posted to Slack.

How it works

A manual run or a weekday schedule (9:00) reads your repositories, lookback window and limits from one settings node.
The Apify node runs fetch_cat/github-issues-pull-requests-scraper once per repository and returns the issues updated in the last 7 days, most recent first. One failed repository is reported and the others continue.
Issues already in your Google Sheet with no new activity are skipped, so nothing is scored twice.
One gpt-5.4-mini call with a strict JSON schema returns, for each issue, a category (bug, regression, security, breaking change, feature or question), a risk score from 1 to 5, whether it affects upgrades and a one-line summary. The answer is validated before anything is written.
Google Sheets gets one row per issue (matched on URL). Issues at risk 4 or higher go to one Slack digest, once each. A quiet day posts nothing.

Setup

Make a copy of the sheet template.
Add the Apify node (verified node on n8n Cloud, @apify/n8n-nodes-apify on self-hosted) and connect your Apify account.
Connect OpenAI, Google Sheets (pick your copy in both Sheets nodes) and Slack (pick a channel).
List your dependencies in 1. Set your watched repositories and run once by hand. Publish the workflow to turn on the weekday schedule.

Setup takes about 10 minutes. A default run (3 repositories, up to 10 issues each) costs about USD 0.02 on Apify plus one small OpenAI call, and maxCostUsdPerRepository caps each Apify run.

Requirements

n8n 2.47.4 or newer with the Apify node
Apify account
OpenAI API key
Google Sheets and Slack accounts

Customization

Change the repositories, lookback window, state, labels and limits in the settings node.
Raise alertMinRiskScore to 5 for only the most severe items, or set includePullRequests to true to score fix pull requests too.
Swap Slack for Teams, Discord or email: the digest is one item with a text field.
Scores use the title, labels, comment and reaction counts and the first part of the issue body, not the full thread, so read the issue before acting.

Appends or updates rows in the Google Sheets Results tab using an auditKey of url plus strategy to avoid duplicates.

Setup
Install the Apify community node @apify/n8n-nodes-apify and create an Apify API token credential in n8n.
Create or copy a Google Sheets file with two tabs named URLs and Results, and ensure the URLs tab includes a url column (or URL/urls/link/page).
Add a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential and replace the spreadsheet ID in both Google Sheets nodes (read and write).
